bands.name: Palmar radiocarpal ligament
bands.mechanical_role: the wrist's strongest capsular ligament; guides the characteristic screw-home-like coupled motion during wrist extension
bands.function_note: Broad, strong palmar band; its integrity is the main reason the palmar wrist capsule is stronger than the dorsal capsule.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

bands.name: Dorsal radiocarpal ligament
bands.mechanical_role: secondary dorsal restraint, weaker than its palmar counterpart
bands.function_note: The thinner, weaker dorsal counterpart to the palmar radiocarpal ligament.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

bands.name: Ulnar collateral ligament of wrist
bands.mechanical_role: resists radial deviation stress; blends with the triangular fibrocartilage complex
bands.function_note: Functionally continuous with the TFCC (see data/cartilage/) rather than a fully separable discrete cord.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

bands.name: Radial collateral ligament of wrist
bands.function_note: Continues distally into the thenar region, blending with the abductor pollicis brevis fascia.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

bands.name: Scapholunate interosseous ligament
bands.mechanical_role: the primary stabilizer of the scapholunate joint; its dorsal region, described by Berger (1996) as thick with short transversely-oriented collagen fibers, is reported by separate biomechanical load-to-failure testing (not this histologic paper itself) as the mechanically strongest of its three regions -- consistent findings from two different kinds of study, not a single paper's claim (precision clarified after adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md)
bands.function_note: Clinically the single most important intrinsic carpal ligament -- its rupture causes scapholunate dissociation (the classic 'Terry Thomas sign' gap on radiographs) and, if untreated, progresses to SLAC (scapholunate advanced collapse) wrist arthritis.
bands.source: Berger RA (1996) 'The gross and histologic anatomy of the scapholunate interosseous ligament.' J Hand Surg Am 21(2):170-178 -- scapholunate ligament's dorsal/palmar/proximal membranous regions and role in carpal stability.

function: The wrist capsule's major thickenings plus the scapholunate interosseous ligament, together maintaining normal carpal alignment and coupled radiocarpal/midcarpal kinematics through wrist flexion-extension and radioulnar deviation.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Berger RA (1996) 'The gross and histologic anatomy of the scapholunate interosseous ligament.' J Hand Surg Am 21(2):170-178 -- scapholunate ligament's dorsal/palmar/proximal membranous regions and role in carpal stability.
